statement.text: Let $A\subset (1,\infty)$ be a countably infinite set such that for all $x eq y\in A$ and integers $k\geq 1$ we have $ \lvert kx -y\rvert \geq 1. $ Does this imply that $A$ is sparse? In particular, does this imply that $ \sum_{x\in A}\frac{1}{x\log x}<\infty $ or $ \sum_{\substack{x <n\\ x\in A}}\frac{1}{x}=o(\log n)? $

title: Erdős Problem #143
